body.p: Applicant has thoroughly reviewed the outstanding final Office Action dated March 26, 2024, and this reply is believed to be fully responsive thereto. Claims 2-4, 6-14, 17, and 19-26 are pending. Claims 1, 3, 5, 15, 16, and 18 have been canceled. Claims 2, 4, 13, and 14 have been amended. Claims 23-26 have been added. No new subject matter has been added. Claims 20-22 have been allowed. Applicant respectfully requests that all remaining claims be allowed and this application pass to issuance in view of the following remarks.

Claims 13 and 14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite. Without conceding to the propriety of this rejection, but rather to expedite prosecution, claims 13 and 14 are amended. This rejection is therefore rendered moot, and withdrawal thereof is thus respectfully requested.

Claims 2-7, 9-14, 17 and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Pub. 2009/0005675 ("Grunwald") in view of U.S. Patent 6,662,055 ("Prutchi") and further in view of U.S. Pub. 2014/0142670 ("Radhakrishnan"). Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Grunwald, Prutchi, Radhakrishnan and still further in view of U.S. Pub. 2015/0173829 ("Lichtenstein").

This rejection is traversed because none of the cited references, either taken alone or in combination, disclose or make obvious each and every feature of independent claim 2. For instance, none of the cited references disclose or make obvious at least "a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member" and a "a sensor disposed at a distal end of the ring electrode."

The Office Action equates the electrical sensing segment 135 shown in Figs. 4A- 4B of Grunwald as equivalent to the claimed electrode of instant independent claim 2. See Office Action, section 11(b). Furthermore, the Office Action equates the distal end 115 of the elongate body 105 as equivalent to the claimed distal end of the elongate member of instant independent claim 2. See Office Action, section 11(a). As shown in Figs. 4A-4B of Grunwald, reproduced below, the electrical sensing segment 135 does not extend from the distal end 115 of the elongate body 105. On the contrary, the electrical sensing segment 135 is shown positioned in the window 170 in order to access blood. See also paragraph [0125]. This window 170 is clearly shown to be proximally located relative to the distal end 115. Thus, Figs. 4A-4B of Grunwald clearly do not show the electrode 135 extending from the distal end 115 of the elongate member 105. Fig. 5A of Grunwald similarly shows the electrical sensing segment 135 extending to a window 170 that is located proximal to the distal end of the elongate member 105, and thus the electrical sensing segment 135 shown in Fig. 5A does not even reach the distal end of the elongate member 105. Accordingly, both Figs. 4 and 5 of Grunwald fail to disclose the electrode 135 extends from the distal end 115 of the elongate member 105.

The Office Action also cites paragraph [0121] of Grunwald as allegedly teaching an electrode that extends from the distal end of the elongate member. This is incorrect. Specifically, paragraph [0121] of Grunwald recites "[e]ndovascular leads 130 (and/or the corresponding electrical sensing segment or segments 135) may extend from the elongate body 105 as shown in FIGS. 2 and 3A or may be integral to or within the elongate body as shown in FIGS. 3B, 4A, 4B 5A, and 5B" (emphasis added).

Regarding Fig. 2 of Grunwald (reproduced below), two separate leads 130 are shown, wherein the first lead is clearly located proximal to the distal end 115, and wherein the second lead is located distal to the distal end 115. However, even though the second lead in this embodiment is located distal to the distal end 115, the ultrasound transducer 120 (which the Office Action equates to the claimed sensor in instant claim 2; see section 11(c)) is not disposed at a distal end of the second lead. On the contrary, the ultrasound transducer 120 is clearly shown to be disposed proximal to the distal end of the second lead (see also paragraphs [0119] and [0120]).

With regard to Fig. 3A of Grunwald, reproduced below, the sensing segment 135 is clearly shown extending through the window 170 which is located proximal to the distal
end 115. Thus, this sensing segment 135 does not extend from the distal end 115 of the elongate body 105.

None of the other cited references make up for these shortcomings of Grunwald. Indeed, Radhakrishnan, which the Office Action relies on to cure deficiencies of Grunwald, discloses a ring structured electrode 114/140 that is disposed proximal to the distal end of the lead body 108, as show in Figs. 1 and 2. Thus, aprimafacie case of obviousness cannot be established with respect to independent claim 2 and any claims depending therefrom. Reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection is therefore respectfully requested.
New Claims

New claims 23-26 are not disclosed or suggested by any of the cited references, either taken alone or together. Accordingly, new independent claim 23 and its dependent claims are believed to be in condition for allowance. Consideration of each new claim on its own merits is respectfully requested.
Claims 2-14, 17, and 19-22 have been rejected for obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854

in view of Grunwald. Independent claim 2 recites various features, such as a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member, that are not recited in claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,006,854 or disclosed in Grunwald for the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of this nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection is respectfully requested.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant submits that all claims are in condition for allowance, and an indication of such is earnestly solicited.

It is believed that all of the pending issues have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Further, Applicants declare that any amendments herein that are not specifically made for the purpose of patentability are made for other purposes, such as clarification, and that no such changes shall be construed as limiting the scope of the claims or the application of the Doctrine of Equivalents. Finally, nothing in this reply should be construed as an intent to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this reply, and the amendment of any claim does not necessarily signify concession of unpatentability of the claim prior to its amendment.
